generation.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: composition-evidence-only whole-world map concept for a 6400x6400 painted JRPG background; never a runtime asset.
Primary request: Generate one coherent square whole-world Meadow Entry concept, using the attached painted-v2 control images as strict geometry and ownership references. Preserve their 6400x6400 master-coordinate composition exactly: region extents, all connected route centerlines and mouths, junctions, open-space widths, interaction clearances, edge handoffs, collision boundaries, and every protected/live, building/transition, and semantic-anchor footprint. The colored geometry masks are instructions only; translate them into clean, readable painted terrain and ground materials, never copy the mask colors or overlay shapes.
Input images: Image 1 is the composite control; Image 2 is the terrain/path mask; Image 3 is the region mask; Image 4 is a temporary combined boundary reference containing the collision mask, building-footprint mask, entrance-transition mask, protected-live mask, and semantic-anchor mask. Treat all of them as geometry controls, not as art.
Scene/backdrop: one continuous orthographic top-down / very slight three-quarter JRPG world map with six readable connected biome masses: cultivated Sundrop Village in the southwest; cobble-and-packed-earth Crossroads at center; cool wet Mistfen marsh in the northwest; autumn Silverpine shrine woods in the north; deep Wildwood forest in the east; bright Tidewatch coast, sand, and sea along the southeast. Keep the whole map visually continuous where regions meet while retaining distinct biome identity.
Style/medium: crisp hand-painted 2D JRPG environment concept, production-game clarity, clean orthographic map readability, crisp shapes and controlled texture; no oil-paint blur, photorealism, or muddy painterly smearing.
Composition/framing: full square world-map view, all outer edges visible, clear route hierarchy at a glance; primary paths are continuous and legible through every region and connector, secondary paths and clearings are calm enough for live NPCs and interactions. Honor the exact control geometry even where it is sparse or abstract.
Lighting/mood: warm late-morning daylight from the upper left, consistent direction across the entire map, gentle contact shading only beneath terrain relief and low dressing; no dramatic cast shadows that imply walls or block routes.
Color palette/materials: Sundrop is warm cultivated greens and golden soil; Crossroads is neutral warm cobble and earth; Mistfen is cool blue-green wet ground with restrained marsh variation; Silverpine is russet, amber, and pine green autumn woodland; Wildwood is deep layered green with subtle forest-floor variation; Tidewatch is bright sunlit sand, turquoise water, and pale coastal accents. Maintain a clear value hierarchy: routes and interaction clearances remain readable against surrounding biome masses.
Constraints: control geometry and live ownership are authoritative; leave every building/transition footprint, protected-live mask area, collision mask area, and semantic-anchor mask area as quiet, flat, unobstructed ground reserved for live runtime objects. Terrain variation may be low and flat around them but cannot create a false wall, curb, doorway, cliff, tall prop, or collision cue. Keep the route mouths and edge handoffs open and calm. Add only low, sparse environmental dressing outside protected/live and anchor areas, with no gameplay-significant object.
Avoid: any baked buildings, roofs, houses, castle gate, Waystone, doors, doorways, lanterns, bridges, shrines, boats, characters, NPCs, enemies, pickups, treasure, discoveries, props at semantic anchors, tall trees blocking paths, false walls, fences, cliffs across routes, labels, lettering, icons, UI, arrows, grid lines, overlays, mask colors, watermarks, logos, repeated tile grids, visible seams, perspective distortion, hard shadows that change gameplay geometry.
